page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-64 is a flexible virtual machine configuration tailored for memory-intensive workloads. It is powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated physical cores supporting 2 threads per core, delivering 8 vCPUs in total. Memory capacity is set to 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU.

Hardware resource allocation on this profile emphasizes system memory over dense compute or graphic acceleration. The instance does not include integrated graphical processing units (0 GPUs) and contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent operating system and application data. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external connectivity.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the flexible allocation model allows users to scale memory up to 64 GB on a relatively modest 4-core physical footprint. This configuration avoids the cost overhead of provisioning unneeded compute cores merely to acquire larger memory capacities. The lack of onboard NVMe storage represents a tradeoff in raw I/O latency, offset by the flexibility to provision decoupled storage pools.

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-64 is suitable for memory-heavy enterprise deployments that do not demand dedicated hardware accelerators. Typical target workloads include relational and in-memory database engines, large cache layers such as Redis or Memcached, data analysis jobs, enterprise enterprise-resource-planning (ERP) modules, and memory-bound backend services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-64 is a flexible compute instance configured for memory-demanding enterprise tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 7J13 processors clocked at 2.55 GHz, the instance delivers 8 vCPUs from 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading support. It features 64.0 GB of system RAM, providing an elevated 8 GB per vCPU allocation that categorizes it as a memory-optimized profile. The instance omits onboard hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs, and includes no local ephemeral storage, meaning persistent storage must be attached over the cloud network. Network access includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The resource profile provides qualitative cost advantages by allowing sizable memory allocation without requiring the purchase of excess vCPUs. It is best aligned with memory-bound workloads, including relational database engines, in-memory caching solutions, and ETL processing pipelines.
